title: The authorisation adapter maps Clerk roles onto project verbs
asA: handler that needs to know whether the caller is allowed to perform an operation
iWant: to call `can(principal, verb)` and receive a boolean decision computed from a project-authored mapping table
soThat: my handler's authorisation check is legible in project vocabulary and swap-safe if the identity vendor changes

acceptanceCriteria.description: The authorisation adapter's `can(principal, verb)` returns `true` when the mapping table grants the verb to at least one role the principal holds, and `false` otherwise.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a mapping table declaring that the verb `article.edit` is granted to roles `editor` and `admin`; a principal whose `roles` array is `['editor']`
acceptanceCriteria.then: the call returns `true`; a second call `can(principal, 'billing.invoice.void')` (a verb not granted to `editor`) returns `false`

acceptanceCriteria.description: The authorisation adapter's `assert(principal, verb)` returns silently on a granted verb and throws a stable-coded `AUTHZ_FORBIDDEN` error naming the verb on a refused one; the error carries no principal claim material.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the same mapping table and principal as AC-9104-1
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first call returns without throwing; the second call throws an `AUTHZ_FORBIDDEN` error whose message contains the string `billing.invoice.void` and whose serialised form contains no role name, no organisation id, and no Clerk claim key or value

acceptanceCriteria.description: A source-tree scan finds no handler code that reads `principal.roles` or `principal.claims` directly; every authorisation check goes through `can` or `assert`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the project's source tree after the blueprint's TACs are realised
acceptanceCriteria.when: a scan enumerates every reference to `.roles`, `.organisationIds`, or `.claims` on an object whose type resolves to the project's `Principal` shape
acceptanceCriteria.then: every match sits inside the authorisation adapter module (TAC-1002) or the claims-mapper module (TAC-1004); no handler file reads a claim directly
